ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an experimental flowchart. The “light green crystal” on the left is added with “dilute H2SO4” to obtain solution (A); then “K2Cr2O7” is added to obtain a “green solution”; after “NaOH (excess)” is added to this green solution, it is divided into two parts: the upper part is (B) “bright green solution”, and the lower part is (C) “red-brown precipitate”. The red-brown precipitate (C) is then treated with “HCl, KNCS” to obtain (D) “blood-red solution”; after “NaF” is added to (D), (E) “colorless solution” is obtained. Reasoning: The light green crystal can be judged to be a ferrous salt, and after dissolving in dilute sulfuric acid, solution (A) containing Fe2+ is obtained. K2Cr2O7 under acidic conditions can oxidize Fe2+ to Fe3+, while itself is reduced to Cr3+, so the green solution contains Fe3+ and Cr3+. After adding excess NaOH, Fe3+ forms a red-brown Fe(OH)3 precipitate, namely (C); Cr3+ forms a soluble chromium hydroxyl complex in excess NaOH, appearing bright green, namely (B). The red-brown Fe(OH)3 precipitate (C) dissolves upon adding HCl to regenerate Fe3+, and then adding KSCN/KNCS forms the blood-red iron(III)-thiocyanate complex (D). After continuing to add NaF, F- has strong coordination ability with Fe3+, replacing or masking SCN-, forming a stable hexafluoroferrate(III) complex ion, therefore the blood-red color fades to become the colorless solution (E). So E is [FeF6]^{3-}.

Determine the substances represented by each letter E according to the following experimental facts:

$\ce{CaCO3 ->[heating] CaO + CO2 \\}$ (E)

$\ce{2Na(s) + 2HCl(aq) ->2NaCl(aq) + H2(g) \\}$ (E)

$\ce{Cu(s) + 4HNO3(aq) ->Cu(NO3)2(aq) + 2NO2(g) + 2H2O(l) \\}$ (E)

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a flowchart of a pale-green crystal undergoing dilute H2SO4 dissolution, dichromate oxidation, excess NaOH separation, then HCl/KSCN and NaF tests. Identify the pale-green crystal as an Fe(II) salt, so after K2Cr2O7 oxidation the solution contains Fe3+ and Cr3+. Use excess NaOH to assign red-brown precipitate C as Fe(OH)3 and bright-green solution B as a chromium hydroxide complex. Dissolve C in acid to regenerate Fe3+, use KSCN to assign D as the blood-red Fe3+-thiocyanate complex, then add NaF and replace/mask SCN- by fluoride coordination to conclude E is [FeF6]^{3-}.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个实验流程图。左侧“淡绿色晶体”加入“稀H2SO4”后得到(A)溶液；再加入“K2Cr2O7”得到“绿色溶液”；该绿色溶液加入“NaOH（过量）”后分成两部分：上方为(B)“亮绿色溶液”，下方为(C)“红棕色沉淀”。红棕色沉淀(C)再经“HCl、KNCS”处理得到(D)“血红色溶液”；(D)加入“NaF”后得到(E)“无色溶液”。推理：淡绿色晶体可判断为亚铁盐，溶于稀硫酸后得到含Fe2+的(A)溶液。K2Cr2O7在酸性条件下能把Fe2+氧化为Fe3+，自身被还原为Cr3+，所以绿色溶液中含Fe3+和Cr3+。加入过量NaOH后，Fe3+生成红棕色Fe(OH)3沉淀，即(C)；Cr3+在过量NaOH中形成可溶的铬羟基配合物，呈亮绿色，即(B)。红棕色Fe(OH)3沉淀(C)加HCl溶解重新生成Fe3+，再加KSCN/KNCS生成血红色铁(III)-硫氰酸根配合物(D)。继续加入NaF后，F-与Fe3+配位能力强，取代或掩蔽SCN-，形成稳定的六氟合铁(III)配离子，因此血红色褪去成为无色溶液(E)。所以E为[FeF6]^{3-}。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an experimental flowchart. The “light green crystal” on the left is added with “dilute H2SO4” to obtain solution (A); then “K2Cr2O7” is added to obtain a “green solution”; after “NaOH (excess)” is added to this green solution, it is divided into two parts: the upper part is (B) “bright green solution”, and the lower part is (C) “red-brown precipitate”. The red-brown precipitate (C) is then treated with “HCl, KNCS” to obtain (D) “blood-red solution”; after “NaF” is added to (D), (E) “colorless solution” is obtained. Reasoning: The light green crystal can be judged to be a ferrous salt, and after dissolving in dilute sulfuric acid, solution (A) containing Fe2+ is obtained. K2Cr2O7 under acidic conditions can oxidize Fe2+ to Fe3+, while itself is reduced to Cr3+, so the green solution contains Fe3+ and Cr3+. After adding excess NaOH, Fe3+ forms a red-brown Fe(OH)3 precipitate, namely (C); Cr3+ forms a soluble chromium hydroxyl complex in excess NaOH, appearing bright green, namely (B). The red-brown Fe(OH)3 precipitate (C) dissolves upon adding HCl to regenerate Fe3+, and then adding KSCN/KNCS forms the blood-red iron(III)-thiocyanate complex (D). After continuing to add NaF, F- has strong coordination ability with Fe3+, replacing or masking SCN-, forming a stable hexafluoroferrate(III) complex ion, therefore the blood-red color fades to become the colorless solution (E). So E is [FeF6]^{3-}.
